items.title: Antonelli leads close FP2: the top five are within 0.321s
items.summary: The official 21-car FP2 classification puts Kimi Antonelli fastest at 1:10.763, 0.253s ahead of Lando Norris; Max Verstappen (+0.259), George Russell (+0.273) and Oscar Piastri (+0.321) complete the top five. Nico Hülkenberg did not set a time. Formula1.com's Saturday Practice Debrief notes the fine margins among the leading teams and asks whether Mercedes can sustain its Friday pace. Stewards' Document 23 lists ten deleted-lap entries for nine drivers (Albon appears twice) after track-use issues at Turns 1 and 4; Race Director's Document 24 sets a below-1:13.0 interval between the Safety Car lines for qualifying and specified reconnaissance laps.
items.why_it_matters: Antonelli leads the Friday sheet, but the top-five spread is only 0.321s and a single-lap classification does not establish race pace. FP3 is the next check on whether Mercedes can stay ahead. The lap-time ruling is not itself a revised classification or a race penalty. The 1:13.0 limit applies only during/after qualifying and on reconnaissance laps while pit exit is open, not to racing laps.

sources.label: FIA: FP2 deleted lap times, Document 23

items.title: Russell gets five-place drop; Camara reprimanded after FP2
items.summary: FIA Document 14 records Russell's sixth ICE against four allowed; the Stewards' separate Document 15 imposes a five-place grid drop. In Document 25, the Stewards found Rafael Camara unnecessarily impeded Charles Leclerc in FP2 and issued Camara his first driving reprimand of the season.
items.why_it_matters: The rulings have different consequences: Russell's sanction affects his Brazil grid position; Camara's reprimand is not a grid penalty. Neither changes the FP2 classification.

items.title: Antonelli's drivers' title is settled; Mercedes still chasing constructors' crown
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli clinched the Drivers' Championship in Mexico. The latest official standings show 380 points for Antonelli and 261 for Verstappen; Mercedes leads Ferrari 630-504. Formula1.com's pre-weekend scenario says Mercedes seals the constructors' title if it gains three points on Ferrari in Brazil.
items.why_it_matters: Brazil's practice has not changed the standings, and the constructors' title remains undecided. These are current pre-race totals, not a result projection.

items.title: Norris reports an early gain from McLaren's Brazil upgrades
items.summary: FIA Document 12 lists four McLaren performance items: front wing, rear wing, beam wing and floor furniture. After Friday practice, Norris said the upgrades seemed to gain performance; he topped FP1 and finished second in FP2. The Race reports that the new front-wing concept is intended to carry into McLaren's 2027 launch specification.
items.why_it_matters: The Friday evidence is encouraging but does not establish a race-long gain. Norris's remarks are a driver assessment; check whether the package remains effective through FP3 and qualifying.

items.title: The Race reports Hamilton is set for a Brazil grid penalty
items.summary: The Race reports Ferrari planned power-unit component changes after FP2 and that Lewis Hamilton is set to take a Brazil grid penalty. The 13:30 UTC FIA refresh found no Hamilton-specific parts report or Stewards' ruling among the 27 discovered event documents.
items.why_it_matters: This is an attributed expectation, not an FIA-confirmed penalty; the exact component and sanction remain unverified. Check the FIA documents before treating a starting position as settled.
